New York City’s specialty coffee, shop by shop

A field guide to the city’s third-wave coffee — the roasters, espresso bars, and multi-roaster cafés pouring single origins with intent, from Bushwick to Harlem, Bay Ridge to Jackson Heights.

100 coffee shops · Manhattan, Brooklyn & Queens · Directory, profiles & map

Browse the directory See the map

What counts as third-wave here

Specialty-grade beans. Single origins, roasted light to medium so the place they grew still tastes like something. Transparent sourcing — you can usually learn who grew the coffee and what was paid for it. And precise brewing, with pour-over and filter taken as seriously as espresso.

That bar leaves out the generic chains and second-wave cafés on purpose. Every shop below clears it, whether it roasts its own beans in the back or pours a rotating cast of roasters from around the world.

Before you go: hours change, and a few of these keep unusual ones. Parlor Coffee’s tasting room is weekend-only (Sat–Sun, 9 AM–3 PM) and Moon Coffee Lab is daytime-only (listings say 8 AM–2 PM) — check both before making the trip, and glance at any shop’s current hours the day you visit.

About this guide

The NYC Coffee Guide was created by Brian Miller, its creator and owner. It is an independent guide to New York City’s specialty coffee shops, built from his own picks and verified research — with Sey Coffee in Bushwick as the benchmark for what counts as third-wave here.

Brian Miller is a Global Advanced Manufacturing Engineer at Vertiv, based in Columbus, Ohio — a manufacturing engineer focused on building systems that last. He studied at Kennesaw State University — Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology.

If the guide helps you find a good cup, a tip is always appreciated — and you can follow along with Brian’s coffee wanderings on Instagram, or connect with him on LinkedIn.

Tip on Venmo Instagram — @brianqzmiller LinkedIn

Addresses and coordinates verified October 29, 2026, against shop listings and the geocoder. The original fifteen shops come from Brian’s verified NYC list; further shops were cross-checked against reputable specialty-coffee guides, including Beean Coffee’s Best Specialty Coffee in NYC 2026, FLTR Magazine’s 2026 New York guide, and Sprudge’s guides to Lower Manhattan and North Brooklyn. The expansion to 100 shops added the Sprudge Lower Manhattan picks not already listed — Drip Coffee Makers in Hudson Square and Brooklyn Heights, and Everyman Espresso’s original East 13th Street café — plus FLTR-cited Mighty Oak Roasters in Astoria and dozens more roasters and multi-roaster cafés, each with a street address checked against shop listings and the geocoder.

Hours change often — confirm before you go, especially for Parlor Coffee and Moon Coffee Lab.
